answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The timber multiplier is published, charged in relic, and dune lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 1449 identities would post 2138 proofs and burn roughly 13 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
